headline: Denver is the assignment after 213 yards and a 3-20 night at Lumen

sectionTitles.currentState: A 5-1 room with a kicking question and a short reset
sectionTitles.gamePlan: How Kansas City attacks a one-point road number in Denver

dek: Kansas City is 5-1 after a 3-20 loss at Seattle, and the next kickoff is at Denver on Sun Nov 1, 3:25 PM CT on CBS with the Chiefs laying 1.5.
videoHook: Seattle just showed the league a 213-yard tape. Denver gets the next swing at it, and Andy Reid's room is a one-point road favorite anyway.
theEdge: ESPN FPI still gives Kansas City 55.7 percent at Denver and DraftKings lists the Chiefs at minus 1.5 on a 40.5 total — a one-score road favorite after an offense that posted 11 first downs and 3-of-11 on third down.

storyline.lede: The next game is Denver, not a replay of Lumen Field. Kansas City walks into Empower Field as a 1.5-point favorite on Sun Nov 1, 3:25 PM CT, CBS, at 5-1, with ESPN FPI at 55.7 percent. Seattle already cashed the blueprint other staffs will study: 24 first downs, 41 rushes for 153 yards, 35:51 of possession, and a 20-3 final.
body: Arrowhead Pride's mailbag is the right question for this week. Will other teams follow Seattle's plan? Denver does not have to copy Sam Darnold's 20-of-28, 96.9-rated day to make Kansas City uncomfortable. It only has to keep Patrick Mahomes off schedule the way Seattle did: seven quarterback hits, one sack, 19-of-33, a 58.3 rating, and an interception by T. Okada. Eric Bieniemy and Andy Reid have six days to put answers on the call sheet before a division road kickoff.

The season is not the 6-11 finish from 2025, and it is not a closed case after one loss. Arrowhead Pride's power-rankings roundup has ESPN sliding the Chiefs from 2 to 4 after the first defeat. That is a media correction, not a roster collapse. The football correction is simpler: 50 rushing yards on 16 attempts and 163 net passing yards will not travel against a team that can sit on a lead. The prior afternoon against the Chargers — 150 rushing yards, 272 net passing yards, 22 first downs, 30:26 of possession in a 22-6 win — is the identity Reid still wants. It is not the tape Denver will defend.

Arrowhead Pride and Arrowhead Addict both report Justin Tucker signed to the practice squad as competition. Special teams is now part of the Denver plan, not a side note. So is the offensive line story around Kingsley Suamataia, whose holding penalty wiped a play in the fourth quarter, and the open question Ian Rapoport has raised about Josh Simmons. None of that changes the number. Kansas City is laying 1.5. It has to play like it.

lastGameReview.label: Week 7 · Sun, Oct 25 · 7:20 PM CT
lastGameReview.lede: At Lumen Field on Sun Oct 25, 7:20 PM CT, Seattle beat Kansas City 20-3. The Seahawks opened the scoring with a 25-yard field goal with 8:22 left in the second quarter, added a 28-yard touchdown with 1:44 left in the half, kicked a 35-yard field goal with 8:09 left in the third, and closed with a 21-yard touchdown with 3:47 left. Kansas City's points were a 50-yard field goal with 1:42 left in the third.

analysis.body: The box is the story. Kansas City had 11 first downs, 213 total yards, eight drives, one turnover, and the ball for 24:09. Seattle had 24 first downs, 410 yards, eight drives, one turnover, and 35:51. Third down was 3-of-11 for the Chiefs and 11-of-16 for Seattle. Arrowhead Pride's third-down piece is right to hang the offensive failure there: drives never became a rhythm.

Mahomes finished 19-of-33 for 165 yards with one interception and a 58.3 rating, and the team net passing line is 163. He was sacked once and absorbed seven quarterback hits. Kansas City recorded two quarterback hits and no sacks on Darnold, who went 20-of-28 with a 96.9 rating. Kenneth Walker III carried 14 times for 36 yards and finished with 18 touches. Travis Kelce tied Kenneth Walker III at four catches and tied Noah Gray at 44 receiving yards. The team rush total was 50 yards on 16 attempts. That is not a run game Denver has to fear until the early-down calls change.

Seattle's explosives were real. With 1:44 left in the second quarter, Darnold hit Jaxon Smith-Njigba on a deep left throw that became a 28-yard touchdown, and the replay reversal confirmed the score. Smith-Njigba finished with 11 touches. Emanuel Wilson carried the grind: 24 rushes and one catch, 25 touches, inside a 41-carry, 153-yard team rush. AJ Barner had seven touches, including a direct-snap rush up the middle on the snap where O. Oluwatimi reported eligible. George Holani added six touches. Steve Spagnuolo's front spent the game fitting a committee, not a single back.

The takeaway ledger is narrow and it belongs to the players on the play list. Mahomes threw short left for J. Royals and T. Okada intercepted, with N. Emmanwori in on the play. N. Williams intercepted Darnold short middle, intended for Rashid Shaheed, and returned it 65 yards, with G. Karlaftis credited on the play. Creed Humphrey's fumble was recovered by Mahomes. Derick Hall forced a fumble on the sack, and Mahomes recovered it. Harrison Butker missed from 58, short, and from 45, wide right, around the 50 he made. A late 4th-and-10 to Kelce for three yards ended in a turnover on downs. Drue Tranquill's 12 tackles and Mansoor Delane's trail work, which Arrowhead Pride flagged as the clean defensive note, were bright spots on a night the scoreboard did not reward.

takeaways.title: Third down decided the yardage gap
takeaways.body: Kansas City was 3-of-11. Seattle was 11-of-16. That is how eight drives apiece became 213 yards against 410 and 24:09 against 35:51. Denver will try to live in that down-and-distance window.

takeaways.title: The run game never became a down-and-distance weapon
takeaways.body: Walker had 14 carries for 36 yards and 18 touches. The team rushed 16 times for 50. Seattle rushed 41 times for 153. Early downs have to look different before third-and-long becomes the Denver plan.

takeaways.title: The scoreboard was field goals until Seattle's two touchdowns
takeaways.body: Seattle scored on a 25-yard field goal, a 28-yard touchdown, a 35-yard field goal, and a 21-yard touchdown. Kansas City's answer was the 50-yard field goal. Butker also missed from 58 and from 45.

whatWorked: N. Williams' interception of Darnold, returned 65 yards, with Karlaftis on the play.
Noah Gray's two 19-yard catches, one deep right and one deep middle, gave Mahomes a middle-of-the-field answer when the vertical shots to Xavier Worthy were incomplete.
Tranquill's 12 tackles and Delane's trail position, noted by Arrowhead Pride, were the defensive details that held up while Seattle still controlled the clock.
whatDidnt: Third-and-long offense: 3-of-11, 11 first downs, eight drives, 213 yards.
The run fit against Wilson's 25 touches and a 41-carry Seattle rush plan. Kansas City had two quarterback hits and no sacks.
Kicking: misses from 58 and 45 around one make from 50, which is why the Tucker practice-squad report is now on the week.

currentState.lede: The Chiefs are 5-1, a one-score road favorite at Denver, and a week removed from their worst offensive yardage line of this season. The staff's job is to keep the Chargers identity — 422 yards, 22 first downs, a 22-6 win — from being treated as ancient history, and to stop Seattle's 20-3 tape from becoming the league's template.

workOn.title: Early-down carries for Walker
workOn.body: Fourteen carries and 36 yards will not stress a defense that can rush four and hit the quarterback seven times. Bieniemy needs Walker on schedule before third down, not as a checkdown after the pocket is already noisy.

workOn.title: Third-down answers under seven hits
workOn.body: Mahomes was 19-of-33 with one sack and seven hits. Quick width to Worthy, Kelce, and Gray has to be the answer before another deep incompletion to Worthy becomes the series.

workOn.title: The kicking competition, in public
workOn.body: Denver's 40.5 total means one kick can swing the 1.5.

thinkAbout.title: Does Denver copy the clock game?
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Pride's mailbag asks whether other teams follow Seattle. A 35:51 possession game with 41 rushes is copyable even if the opponent quarterback is not Darnold. Spagnuolo has to tackle the run on first down or the same third-down math returns.

thinkAbout.title: Does one loss rewrite the scouting report?
thinkAbout.body: ESPN FPI still hangs 55.7 percent on the Denver trip and DraftKings still lists Kansas City minus 1.5. That is a lean after one loss, not a scouting report. The scouting report is 213 yards and 3-of-11.

thinkAbout.title: What is real about the tackle depth?
thinkAbout.body: Suamataia's holding penalty wiped a fourth-quarter play. Arrowhead Addict reports Ian Rapoport raising doubts about Josh Simmons playing for the Chiefs again. Reid cannot treat tackle stability as settled heading into a division road game.

gamePlan.lede: Denver is the assignment: a division road game on Sun Nov 1, 3:25 PM CT, CBS, with Kansas City laying 1.5 on a 40.5 total and FPI at 55.7 percent. The Broncos get a rested look at a 3-20 tape. Kansas City has to steal the script back before Denver sits on early-down runs and third-and-long.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Seattle won with volume rushing, third-down efficiency, and explosives to Smith-Njigba. Denver does not need that personnel to borrow the idea. Kansas City's leverage is still Mahomes, Kelce (four catches, 44 yards), Gray's 19-yard answers, Worthy on the perimeter, and Walker if the carries come before the down-and-distance gets ugly. Spagnuolo's leverage is fitting the run with the tacklers ESPN logged: Tranquill (12), Nick Bolton (11), Nohl Williams (10), Jack Cochrane, Khyiris Tonga, and George Karlaftis. Give Denver credit: home field, a one-score number, and a clear film study of how to keep Mahomes at 11 first downs.

keys.title: Win first down so third down is not 3-of-11 again
keys.body: Inside zone and a defined screen keep Walker, who had 18 touches, from becoming a 14-carry, 36-yard afterthought. If Denver plays the Seattle rush-four plan, the ball has to come out before the seventh hit.

keys.title: Take the deep middle without living there
keys.body: Worthy had three catches and three charted incompletions deep. Gray was the completion. Mesh and a boot give Kelce and Gray the easy answers; four verticals is a shot, not the identity.

keys.title: Rally fits on early-down runs
keys.body: Cover 2 takes away the shot Seattle hit for 28 yards to Smith-Njigba. A zone blitz is a call to change the picture on third down, not a claim that pressure created either interception.

keys.title: Treat the kick as a possession weapon
keys.body: A 40.5 total and a 1.5 spread mean Butker's 50-yard make and the two misses are game-plan facts. Do not ask for 58 if the drive can steal four.

script: Open with under-center inside zone to Walker and a shotgun check to Kelce so Denver cannot sit in the Seattle third-and-long look.
Call the screen to Walker on an early second-and-medium if the rush shows the same heat that produced seven hits.
Use mesh versus man on third-and-4 to 6, with Worthy on the corner route and Gray as the sit.
Save four verticals for a clean pocket look after a run fake has moved a safety, not as the answer to pressure.
Play Cover 2 on early downs against a shot team that just watched Smith-Njigba win deep left.
Call the zone blitz on a Denver third-and-medium, dropping a defensive lineman and rushing the second level, with Karlaftis and Tranquill as the fitters.

spotlight.title: A one-point favorite with a 213-yard tape
spotlight.body: DraftKings has Kansas City minus 1.5. ESPN FPI has the Chiefs at 55.7 percent. That is a lean, not a mandate, after Seattle posted 410 yards and 35:51.

spotlight.title: 3-of-11 is the number Denver will chase
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride centered the Seattle loss on third-down failure. Eight drives and 11 first downs will not beat a team that can play keep-away.

spotlight.title: Tucker is on the practice squad
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride and Arrowhead Addict report Justin Tucker signed while Butker missed from 58 and 45 and made from 50. The 40.5 total makes that a Denver variable.

spotlight.title: Still laying 1.5 after a 3-20
spotlight.body: DraftKings has Kansas City minus 1.5. ESPN FPI has the Chiefs at 55.7 percent. That is a lean, not a mandate, ahead of Sun Nov 1, 3:25 PM CT.

spotlight.title: ESPN moved Kansas City from 2 to 4
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride's Week 8 roundup logged the drop after the first loss. Walker is still the best-offseason-addition note in that same sampling. He needs carries that match the label.

matchups.unit: Chiefs early-down run vs. a defense that just watched 50 yards
matchups.chiefs: Kenneth Walker III, 14 carries, 36 yards, 18 touches; team rush 50 on 16
matchups.opponent: A Denver front that can sit on the Seattle tape and dare Kansas City to throw on third-and-long
matchups.note: Until the carry count and the yards move together, the run is the side Denver can crowd.

matchups.chiefs: Patrick Mahomes, 19-of-33, 165 yards, 1 INT, 1 sack, 7 QB hits, rating 58.3
matchups.opponent: Whatever rush Denver borrows from a game that produced seven hits and one sack
matchups.note: The quick game has to travel. Another 19-of-33 day on the road is how a 1.5 favorite becomes a one-score loser.

matchups.unit: Kelce and Gray vs. intermediate coverage
matchups.chiefs: Travis Kelce, 4 receptions, 44 yards; Noah Gray, two 19-yard completions on the play list
matchups.opponent: Denver's linebackers and safeties, asked to squeeze crossers after Seattle took away explosives
matchups.note: Gray was the completed deep answer. Kelce remains the third-down target, including the three-yard catch that ended a drive on downs.

matchups.unit: Spagnuolo's run fit vs. a copycat ground game
matchups.chiefs: Drue Tranquill, 12 tackles; two team QB hits and no sacks on Darnold
matchups.opponent: Seattle's model: 41 rushes, 153 yards, Emanuel Wilson 25 touches, 11-of-16 on third down
matchups.note: Kansas City can tackle. It did not sack the quarterback or steal the clock. Denver gets a real edge if it runs on first down and Kansas City cannot create a third-and-long of its own.

matchups.chiefs: Harrison Butker made from 50, missed from 58 and 45; Justin Tucker on the practice squad per club reporting
matchups.opponent: A one-score home environment where one kick covers the 1.5
matchups.note: The make from 50 shows the leg. The two misses are why the competition exists. Do not over-credit either side until Sunday's kickers are the ones on the field.

xsandos.title: Walker downhill before the down gets long
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10 early, at Denver, before the defense can replay Seattle's third-and-long rush
xsandos.why: Kansas City rushed for 50 yards on 16 attempts, and Walker had 14 of those carries for 36 yards. Denver will expect Mahomes to throw into seven-hit math. An under-center zone carry gives Walker a one-cut downhill look and gives Bieniemy a down that is not already third-and-7.
xsandos.coaching: Reid and Bieniemy: call it under center, zone steps, one cut. Walker presses the point of attack and bends off the first free hat. Do not wait for shotgun on every early down the way the Lumen tape lived in shotgun.

xsandos.title: Screen the rush that produced seven hits
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-6 to 8 after a modest gain, if Denver shows four heat
xsandos.why: Mahomes took seven quarterback hits and one sack. Walker already has the hands for a four-catch game. A screen lets the line get out in space and turns pressure into a catch-and-run instead of another incompletion deep to Worthy.
xsandos.coaching: Bieniemy: sell the five-step, then let the guards and the back work the same side. Walker catches on the move. Kelce stays in to help if the end crashes. This is an answer to hits, not a shot play.

xsandos.title: Mesh for Kelce on third-and-medium
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-4 to 6, the down Seattle won 11 times in 16 tries
xsandos.why: Kansas City was 3-of-11 on third down and Kelce tied Gray at 44 receiving yards, with Walker also catching four. A rub gives him a window against man, with Worthy on the corner and Gray sitting if the linebacker chases the crosser.
xsandos.coaching: Kelce and Gray cross at depth with timing, not a scramble drill. Worthy bends the corner. Walker is the checkdown if both crossers are squeezed. Mahomes throws the first open window, the way the three-yard Kelce ball on the late drive needed more than three yards of separation.

xsandos.title: Boot after the run has been honored
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-5 on the opening drive, once Walker has a carry on the sheet
xsandos.why: This is a call for Denver, not a label on the Seattle throws. The Lumen tape did not give Denver a boot to study. Selling Walker, then moving Mahomes to the perimeter, is how Reid changes the picture after a pocket that absorbed seven hits.
xsandos.coaching: Under center, sell the zone, boot Mahomes away from the rush. Kelce leaks to the flat. Gray runs the over. Worthy stretches the corner. Mahomes takes the flat if the second level sits.

xsandos.title: Cover 2 against the shot Seattle just hit
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10 after a Denver completion, protecting the deep left that became a 28-yard touchdown
xsandos.why: Smith-Njigba's 28-yard touchdown and his 11 touches are the film Denver's offense will enjoy. Two deep safeties take the go-ball off the table and let Tranquill, who had 12 tackles, rally with Bolton and Cochrane.
xsandos.coaching: Spagnuolo: two deep, five under. Corners jam and sink. Safeties stay on top of the vertical. Linebackers fit the run so a 41-carry plan cannot be repeated. This shell is about rally tackles, not a gambling single-high look.

xsandos.title: Zone blitz on third-and-medium
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-5 to 7, Denver in shotgun, Kansas City needing a stop that does not give up the shot
xsandos.why: Seattle converted 11 of 16 third downs while Kansas City recorded two quarterback hits and no sacks. The zone blitz is a call to change the rush picture in Denver. It is not a claim that a blitz created Williams' interception or Okada's.
xsandos.coaching: Show heat, drop a defensive lineman into the hook, and rush a second-level player. Karlaftis sets an edge. Tranquill triggers only if the call sends him. The dropper has to carry the crosser so a checkdown does not become a first down the way Seattle's short game did.

playmakers.name: Drue Tranquill
playmakers.role: second-level rusher or hook, by the call

coaching.topic: Reid and Bieniemy vs. the Seattle template
coaching.detail: The mailbag question is the week: other teams will try to keep Mahomes in third-and-long. The answer is early-down runs and defined quick game, not more 19-of-33 volume.

Two quarterback hits and no sacks will not steal a 35:51 game. Fits from Tranquill, Bolton, Tonga, and Cochrane have to win first down so the zone blitz is a changeup, not the only way to get off the field.

coaching.topic: Special teams is on the call sheet
coaching.detail: Butker made from 50 and missed from 58 and 45. Tucker is practice-squad competition per Arrowhead Pride. In a 40.5 game, Reid should know the makeable kick before the drive starts.

personnel.move: Justin Tucker signed to the practice squad
personnel.detail: Arrowhead Pride and Arrowhead Addict report Tucker brought in as competition for Harrison Butker after the misses in Seattle. Butker remains the kicker who made the 50 and missed from 58 and 45 until the club says otherwise.

personnel.move: Josh Simmons future questioned in reporting
personnel.detail: Arrowhead Addict cites Ian Rapoport raising doubts about Simmons playing for the Chiefs again. That is a reported question, not a Week 8 availability line. Suamataia's holding penalty is the on-field tackle note from the Seattle game.

strategies: Steal first down with Walker so Denver cannot live in the 3-of-11 window.
Throw the screen and the mesh before asking Worthy to win another deep ball into tight coverage.
Use Cover 2 on early downs to take away the 28-yard shot Seattle just scored.
Call the zone blitz as a third-down changeup, with a dropper assigned to the checkdown.
Bank field goals inside Butker's made range and avoid another 58-yard try if four yards of field position are available.
Keep Kelce and Gray as the intermediate answers; they were the completed answers when the explosives were not.
debates: Does a 1.5 road number overrate a team that just managed 213 yards?
Should Bieniemy script Walker on the first three early downs, even if Denver loads the box?
Is Tucker a real Week 8 factor, or a practice-squad message to Butker?
If Denver copies the 41-carry plan, is Cover 2 enough or does Spagnuolo have to live in the zone blitz?
Does the ESPN drop from 2 to 4 change how you watch a 5-1 team?
